7.title: Customer interface
7.desc: Where customers and businesses initiate payments, see balances and receive confirmations.
7.caution: The front-end product does not by itself establish who holds the funds or which institution settles.
subs: Mobile and web experiences that initiate transfers and display available balances.
Distinguish product owner from the entity legally holding the customer balance.
Interfaces that allow a business to instruct transfers or offer payments inside another product.
An API provider may orchestrate a bank relationship rather than operate a rail.
The place where a shopper chooses a payment method and authorizes a purchase.
Checkout is not the same as card acquiring or interbank settlement.
The customer-facing ledger, transaction history and available balance.
Displayed balances can represent deposits, e-money or other claims.

6.title: Last mile
6.desc: The local delivery mechanism that makes value available to the recipient.
6.caution: Payout availability, receiving-account credit and interbank settlement may happen at different times.
subs: Credits the recipient through a bank or payment institution in the destination market.
Recipient institution may be distinct from the cross-border provider.
Credits a licensed wallet or e-money provider.
The wallet customer claim and underlying trust or safeguarding account are different.
Uses an agent network to pay out notes to a verified recipient.
An agent may hold local cash inventory or receive reimbursement from a network.
Delivers to an eligible card-linked account using participating issuer and network arrangements.
Availability depends on scheme rules, issuer, market and card type.

5.title: FX and liquidity
5.desc: Currency conversion and the funding needed to complete domestic and cross-border legs.
5.caution: FX pricing, execution, prefunding and rebalancing are different functions.
subs: Quotes and exchanges one currency for another when a payment requires conversion.
A same-currency cross-border payment may require no FX conversion.
Keeps usable funds on the payout side so a transfer can be paid before offsetting funds arrive.
Prefunded liquidity can be replenished separately from the customer transfer.
Manages positions across accounts, currencies and banking partners.
A later treasury transfer is not necessarily the recipient payment.
Provides intraday or settlement liquidity to eligible participants.
A settlement account and access to liquidity are different capabilities.

4a.title: Schemes and networks
4a.desc: Rules, eligibility, addressing, routing and messaging connecting payment participants.
4a.caution: A network may transmit instructions or set scheme rules without holding customer money.
subs: Defines card transaction rules and operates card-network services.
Differentiate network operator, issuer, acquirer and issuer processor.
Sets rules for local account-to-account payment instructions.
Interac is a network; participating institutions hold customer accounts.
Carries standardized payment instructions between institutions and infrastructures.
Swift does not hold funds or settle payment obligations.
Links payment participants for near-real-time payment exchange and, depending on design, settlement.
Direct connection and direct settlement may have different eligibility.
Records and validates token movements subject to a network protocol.
A blockchain is not identical to the reserve issuer, custodian or redemption bank.

4b.title: Processing
4b.desc: Software and operational services that authorize, route, ledger, clear and reconcile payments.
4b.caution: Technology providers can connect directly to a network without being the bank that holds the balance.
subs: Runs transaction authorization, card controls and issuer program records.
The licensed issuing bank retains its separate obligations.
Handles merchant-side payment authorization and submission for clearing.
Processor and acquiring bank should appear as separate roles.
Maintains account-level postings and available balances for a licensed provider.
An internal ledger entry is not by itself central-bank settlement.
Computes obligations and matches payment records before or after settlement.
ACSS calculates net obligations which are settled separately.
Chooses a route, validates requests and manages retries between providers.
Do not assume the orchestrator ever takes custody of funds.

3.title: Multi-market accounts
3.desc: Account-like products spanning jurisdictions and currencies, often combining several underlying legal entities and banking partners.
3.caution: A brand offering worldwide balances is not necessarily one licensed legal company.
subs: Provides local account details or collection capabilities for incoming payments.
Account details and legal ownership of deposits must be checked separately.
Shows and manages balances across currencies in one customer experience.
The underlying holding model can differ by jurisdiction.
Offers the operational account layer behind a multi-market product.
It can involve licensed e-money entities, banks or partner institutions.
Uses accounts and payment partners in multiple destinations.
Payout reach does not prove a direct settlement account in every destination.

2a.title: Correspondents
2a.desc: Banks and settlement providers that maintain accounts and payments connectivity for other institutions across markets.
2a.caution: Cross-border payments can involve separate nostro/vostro positions and messaging legs.
subs: A bank holds an account with another bank to support foreign-currency payments.
The currency of an account does not imply it is held at that currency’s central bank.
Allows an institution to access domestic clearing of another currency through partners.
Sponsorship or a correspondent may be needed even without FX conversion.
Passes payment instructions and funding across one or more banking relationships.
Actual routing may be private; diagrams must not invent named links.

2b.title: Sponsor banks
2b.desc: Banks that supply accounts, scheme participation or settlement agency to firms that lack those capabilities themselves.
2b.caution: Banking-as-a-service, customer deposits and scheme sponsorship should not be merged.
subs: Supplies deposit or payment accounts behind another company’s customer experience.
Check the customer contract for the actual deposit-taking entity.
Supplies eligible network participation for a client program or indirect participant.
A sponsorship relationship is distinct from providing processing software.
Settles obligations for an indirect payment-system participant through the agent’s eligible account.
FedNow explicitly distinguishes correspondent settlement from technical service providers.

1.title: Settlement systems
1.desc: The infrastructure and account arrangements where inter-institution obligations become final.
1.caution: Finality can occur in central-bank money or other agreed settlement arrangements, not always on one central-bank ledger.
subs: Settles obligations individually through a system such as Lynx, CHAPS or Fedwire.
An RTGS account belongs to the eligible participant, not every payment-app customer.
Nets multiple payment obligations and settles the resulting positions in a later cycle.
Retail payments can appear immediate before underlying net settlement.
Provides settlement balances to eligible institutions under system-specific access conditions.
Having settlement access is not equivalent to permission to safeguard customer funds.
Marks the point where the relevant settlement obligation becomes irrevocable under system rules.
Customer credit and legal finality are not necessarily simultaneous.
Transfers between customers on the same institution’s books without requiring a new interbank transfer for that transfer.
The bank still has separate funding and settlement obligations elsewhere.

banking-as-service.desc: Supplies deposit or payment accounts behind another company’s customer experience.
banking-as-service.caution: Check the customer contract for the actual deposit-taking entity.

wise.name: Wise
wise.desc: Multi-currency accounts, payment initiation, FX and payout services.
wise.caution: A Wise-branded service may use different group entities, bank partners and safeguarding arrangements by market. No single role applies globally.

visa.name: Visa
visa.desc: Card-network rules and acceptance infrastructure, with payout and processing-related services.
visa.caution: Visa operates network services; customer deposits are held by issuing institutions, not the card network as such.

mastercard.name: Mastercard
mastercard.desc: Card scheme and switching network providing authorization, clearing and settlement-related network services.
mastercard.caution: Mastercard manages network clearing and settlement functions, but an issuer or acquirer is the account-holding institution. Do not mistake the scheme for a central bank.

swift.name: Swift
swift.desc: Secure standardized financial messaging used by banks and market infrastructures.
swift.caution: Swift is neither a payment nor settlement system and does not hold customer funds.

interac.name: Interac
interac.desc: Operator of Canadian payment services including Interac e-Transfer. Funds stay at participating institutions.
interac.caution: Interac says it does not hold the funds transferred through e-Transfer: the customer relationship and accounts are at participating institutions.

marqeta.name: Marqeta
marqeta.desc: Issuing processing technology and related card-program management services.
marqeta.caution: Marqeta is not the issuing bank; its program offerings rely on issuing-bank partners.

clearbank.name: ClearBank
clearbank.desc: Banking accounts and direct payment-scheme access for business and fintech clients.
clearbank.caution: The company states direct participation in UK and EU schemes; do not infer that any particular client settles in its own account.

circle.name: Circle
circle.desc: Issuer of USDC and administrator of its reserves and redemption arrangements.
circle.caution: A stablecoin issuer is not the blockchain network, the reserve custodian or the final settlement ledger for every holder.

payments-canada.name: Payments Canada
payments-canada.desc: Operator of Lynx, ACSS and the planned RTR in Canada.
payments-canada.caution: System operator and central bank are separate; Lynx participants maintain Bank of Canada settlement accounts.

bank-of-canada.name: Bank of Canada
bank-of-canada.desc: Central-bank settlement account provider and overseer of key payment systems.
bank-of-canada.caution: RTR settlement-account eligibility policy does not prove RTR is live or identify a specific live non-bank settlement customer.

federal-reserve.name: Federal Reserve
federal-reserve.desc: Operates Fedwire Funds, FedNow and FedACH, and holds master accounts for eligible institutions.
federal-reserve.caution: Eligible FedNow participants may use their own master account or a correspondent arrangement; service providers can provide technical connectivity.

banco-central-do-brasil.name: Banco Central do Brasil
banco-central-do-brasil.desc: Operates Pix components, including SPI settlement infrastructure and DICT addressing.
banco-central-do-brasil.caution: BCB distinguishes direct settlement participants from indirect participants; direct Pix service availability is not proof of direct SPI access.

canada.title: Canada
canada.headline: Strong domestic rails; RTR is planned, not yet confirmed live.
canada.intro: Interac e-Transfer, ACSS and Lynx occupy different parts of the Canadian infrastructure. Payments Canada targets an RTR launch in Q4 2026; launch and participant names must be rechecked after that point.
nodes: A customer-facing network service; Interac says it does not hold transferred funds.
Retail batch clearing and net settlement calculations; USD clearing can use USBE.
High-value CAD RTGS. Payments Canada operates it; participants maintain Bank of Canada settlement accounts.
Holds eligible participant settlement accounts, subject to account policies.
New real-time system in sequenced launch phase; not shown as live.

united-states.title: United States
united-states.headline: Multiple rails, different access and settlement models.
united-states.intro: FedNow supports banks and eligible financial institutions, settlement agents/correspondents and technical service providers. Eligibility to use FedNow differs from having a master account.
nodes: Instant-payment infrastructure operated by Federal Reserve Banks.
An eligible participant can use its own master account or a correspondent for settlement.
Technical service providers may transmit messages for participants without being settlement account holders.
Settlement recorded in the relevant Reserve Bank account arrangement.

uk.title: United Kingdom
uk.headline: Non-bank PSPs may obtain direct settlement access under conditions.
uk.intro: The Bank of England has allowed eligible non-bank PSPs to apply for RTGS settlement accounts since 2017. CHAPS directly settles payment obligations in RTGS, while Faster Payments also has directly-connected non-settling participants.
nodes: Fast retail payment exchange; connection and settlement roles can differ.
High-value payment system with individual settlement on BoE RTGS books.
Directly eligible participants can hold settlement accounts.
Bank provides direct scheme access and infrastructure services to clients.

brazil.title: Brazil
brazil.headline: Pix distinguishes scheme participation from direct SPI settlement.
brazil.intro: Banco Central do Brasil operates Pix infrastructure. Eligible authorized institutions may participate directly in SPI, while other institutions settle indirectly through a direct participant or agent.
nodes: Rules and alias directory supporting instant payments.
Interbank instant-payment settlement in dedicated PI accounts.
Hold applicable SPI accounts and settle Pix obligations directly.
Rely on eligible direct participants or settlement agents.

mexico.title: Mexico
mexico.headline: SPEI connects financial institutions for local peso transfers.
mexico.intro: Banco de México operates SPEI, a 24/7 real-time settlement system in Mexican pesos, and publishes participant and indirect-participation information.
nodes: Banco de México-operated interbank electronic transfer system.
Access can be through the supported indirect participation arrangements.

ecuador.title: Ecuador
ecuador.headline: USD denomination does not make this a domestic U.S. payment.
ecuador.intro: Ecuador uses USD, while Banco Central del Ecuador separately operates a domestic interbank payment system (SPI). A payment originating in the United States may still require cross-border banking relationships and local payout. No named correspondent chain is asserted.
nodes: Local USD customer claim or account; not inherently a deposit at the U.S. Federal Reserve.
Possible correspondent or funded partner; actual route must be documented.
Local delivery to the recipient account.
The central bank operates domestic interbank payment infrastructure in Ecuador; this is not Fedwire.

india.title: India
india.headline: UPI operated by NPCI; settlement infrastructure at RBI.
india.intro: Separate app, PSP, bank account, network and settlement.

on-us.title: On-us transfer
on-us.subtitle: Same institution · internal transfer
on-us.desc: When payer and recipient are customers of the same provider, the provider may update its own ledger without a new interbank transfer for that transaction.
on-us.caution: Verified system rule; example path conceptual

canada-domestic.title: Canada · CAD account transfer
canada-domestic.subtitle: Canada → Canada · CAD
canada-domestic.desc: Illustrates separate bank customer accounts, Interac instruction exchange and underlying bank settlement arrangements. Not a claim of a single fixed path for all e-Transfers.
canada-domestic.caution: Illustrative — do not equate e-Transfer notifications with ACSS settlement timing

us-ecuador.title: USD → USD across borders
us-ecuador.subtitle: United States → Ecuador · USD
us-ecuador.desc: Both ends can be denominated in USD, while separate jurisdictions and banks still matter. This is a role-level example, not a verified named correspondent chain.
us-ecuador.caution: Illustrative — named route is not verified

card-purchase.title: Card purchase
card-purchase.subtitle: Cardholder → merchant
card-purchase.desc: Distinguishes merchant checkout, acquiring-side services, card network processing, issuer authorization, and later clearing / settlement.
card-purchase.caution: Conceptual network path; not every card payment uses same processors

cross-border-fx.title: Cross-border FX payout
cross-border-fx.subtitle: USD → PHP · illustrative
cross-border-fx.desc: Shows collection in one currency, conversion/liquidity and local payout. Local balances can be prefunded, with separate treasury replenishment.
cross-border-fx.caution: Illustrative — no specific live partnership inferred

stablecoin.title: Stablecoin transfer
stablecoin.subtitle: USDC · on-chain transfer
stablecoin.desc: Shows wallet transfer on a token network separately from issuer reserve assets and redemption back to a bank account.
stablecoin.caution: Conceptual, chain and redemption rules vary

ca-us.title: Canada → United States
ca-us.subtitle: CAD → USD · cross-border
ca-us.desc: Example of two local markets connected by banking and FX arrangements. One branded product need not own every underlying leg.
ca-us.caution: Illustrative — not a verified end-to-end named route

central-bank.title: At the central bank
central-bank.desc: Eligible participant has an account with a central bank.
central-bank.caution: This is normally the settlement asset/account of an eligible institution, not the individual app customer’s deposit.

bank-deposit.title: As a bank deposit
bank-deposit.desc: A customer has a deposit claim against a deposit-taking bank.
bank-deposit.caution: The deposit insurer and legal depositor matter; a banking app is not necessarily the bank.

pooled-fbo.title: In one pooled account (FBO)
pooled-fbo.desc: A bank holds an omnibus/FBO deposit while a separate program ledger tracks individual end-user entitlements.
pooled-fbo.caution: FBO describes an account and recordkeeping arrangement; it is not a distinct settlement asset.

safeguarded.title: Safeguarded by the company
safeguarded.desc: A payment or e-money entity protects customer funds separately from its operating funds.
safeguarded.caution: Funds may be held as cash, secure assets or other permitted methods depending on entity and jurisdiction.

invested.title: Backed by permitted investments
invested.desc: An entity holds permitted liquid assets against customer balances.
invested.caution: These investments can coexist with safeguarding; they are not always a customer bank deposit.

trust.title: In trust at a local bank
trust.desc: Customer or wallet value is supported by money held in a trust arrangement.
trust.caution: Trust beneficiary and local payout rules depend on the jurisdiction; this is not always a single pooled FBO account.

stablecoin-reserves.title: Behind a stablecoin
stablecoin-reserves.desc: Reserves are usually split across several institutions. For USDC, Circle issues the token, most reserves sit in a BlackRock-managed government money market fund whose custodian is BNY Mellon, and the rest is cash at banks. Other stablecoins are set up differently.
stablecoin-reserves.caution: Reserve backing is distinct from the token transfer network and from the bank where redemption takes place.

policy: Illustrative routes must not be presented as verified bank-to-bank relationships.

payments-canada.title: Payments Canada
payments-canada.overview: A single operator owns and operates Lynx and ACSS and is developing RTR. The Bank of Canada supplies the central-bank settlement accounts.
payments-canada.owns: Payments Canada is a not-for-profit organization created by federal law and funded by members. It is not a shareholder-owned private bank network.
payments-canada.rules: Payments Canada owns and operates Lynx and ACSS, including associated rules and standards.
payments-canada.settles: Eligible direct participants hold settlement accounts on Bank of Canada books. Payments Canada does not itself become the central bank.
payments-canada.access: Membership eligibility is distinct from being a direct participant and from actually holding a settlement account.

interac.title: Interac
interac.overview: Interac operates e-Transfer and debit infrastructure. Its shareholders include banks, credit unions, caisses populaires and payment acquirers.
interac.owns: Interac describes a diverse shareholder base of financial-services entities. Shareholding is not the same as e-Transfer participation, and not every bank is necessarily a shareholder.
interac.rules: Interac runs e-Transfer operational and network services; financial institutions can be direct connectors, indirect connectors or downstream entities with different arrangements.
interac.settles: Interac does not itself hold e-Transfer customers’ balances; financial institutions provide accounts and clearing/settlement arrangements.
interac.access: The public disclosure distinguishes direct and indirect connectors, participants and downstream entities.

us-federal-reserve.title: Federal Reserve payment services
us-federal-reserve.type: Public central-bank system with a distinctive federal structure
us-federal-reserve.overview: Fedwire, FedACH and FedNow are separate services in the Federal Reserve payments family, not interchangeable rails.
us-federal-reserve.owns: The Federal Reserve System is not a conventional shareholder-owned corporation; the Board is a federal agency and regional Reserve Banks have a distinct statutory structure.
us-federal-reserve.rules: Federal Reserve Banks operate core payment services subject to applicable Federal Reserve rules and procedures.
us-federal-reserve.settles: Federal Reserve accounts settle relevant obligations. Direct service access and use of a correspondent/settlement agent must be evaluated separately.
us-federal-reserve.access: FedNow participants, settlement agents, liquidity providers and certified technology service providers have distinct roles.

us-clearing-house.title: The Clearing House
us-clearing-house.overview: The Clearing House operates RTP, CHIPS and EPN, offering private-sector alternatives or complements to Federal Reserve services.
us-clearing-house.owns: The Clearing House identifies itself as owned by major commercial banks. Ownership alone does not imply that a bank must be an owner to participate in each system.
us-clearing-house.rules: Each of RTP, CHIPS and EPN has its own technical arrangements, operating requirements and payment characteristics.
us-clearing-house.settles: RTP provides instant interbank settlement; CHIPS provides high-value clearing and settlement; EPN is an ACH operator under ACH rules.
us-clearing-house.access: Ownership, scheme membership, system participation and access through service providers are distinct.

us-ach.title: ACH governance across operators
us-ach.type: Shared industry rules; public and private ACH operators
us-ach.overview: ACH is a particularly useful case: Nacha governs the common rulebook, while the Federal Reserve and The Clearing House operate the two ACH processing networks.
us-ach.owns: Neither Nacha nor the ACH concept is equivalent to a single company owning every ACH rail.
us-ach.rules: Nacha develops and administers ACH rules. Operating responsibilities belong to the Federal Reserve and EPN (The Clearing House).
us-ach.settles: The operators process ACH files and settlement is effected between relevant financial institutions through applicable settlement arrangements.
us-ach.access: Originators, third-party senders, ODFIs, RDFIs and ACH operators have separate roles.

brazil-pix.title: Pix / Banco Central do Brasil
brazil-pix.overview: Pix’s scheme owner and key infrastructure operator is the same central bank, unlike the separately governed networks in some other markets.
brazil-pix.owns: Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) is the scheme owner; this refers to governance of Pix, not ownership of deposit balances held at participant institutions.
brazil-pix.rules: BCB defines the Pix rulebook, supervises scheme participation and operates the DICT alias directory.
brazil-pix.settles: BCB operates SPI, its instant-payment RTGS settlement infrastructure. Direct and indirect SPI participation must be distinguished.
brazil-pix.access: A payment institution can offer Pix through indirect settlement; customer access to Pix does not prove direct SPI membership.

uk-payuk.title: Pay.UK retail payment systems
uk-payuk.overview: Pay.UK operates Faster Payments and Bacs. It is separate from the Bank of England, whose RTGS accounts settle net obligations.
uk-payuk.owns: The operator and settlement-service provider are distinct organizations; this is the important governance boundary at this level.
uk-payuk.rules: Pay.UK operates retail schemes. Service availability to customers does not imply an RTGS settlement account at the Bank of England.
uk-payuk.settles: Faster Payments and Bacs settle net obligations through the Bank of England’s RTGS infrastructure on separate settlement cycles.
uk-payuk.access: Eligible institutions may access certain schemes directly while relying on another firm for settlement.

uk-boe.title: Bank of England settlement and CHAPS
uk-boe.type: Central-bank owned and operated settlement infrastructure
uk-boe.overview: The Bank of England runs the RTGS infrastructure and operates CHAPS, distinct from Pay.UK’s retail systems.
uk-boe.owns: The Bank of England is the central-bank provider of sterling RTGS and the operator of CHAPS.
uk-boe.rules: The Bank’s RTGS/CHAPS governance sets the operating framework for these systems.
uk-boe.settles: CHAPS settles individually in real time; other retail systems settle net obligations on different cycles in RTGS.
uk-boe.access: Eligible non-bank PSPs may apply for RTGS settlement access but access is not an automatic grant.

india-npci.title: NPCI / UPI
india-npci.overview: NPCI owns and operates the UPI network; banks act as PSPs and account providers, while customer-facing third-party apps can be separate.
india-npci.owns: NPCI is a not-for-profit organization with a shareholder base including banks and other authorized payment-sector institutions; do not treat NPCI as the RBI.
india-npci.rules: NPCI owns the UPI network and prescribes its participant operating arrangements.
india-npci.settles: NPCI is the clearing and settlement agency. It calculates each bank's net position and submits it to RBI's RTGS as a net settlement batch, which debits and credits members' settlement accounts at RBI. The customer sees the money instantly, while interbank settlement happens later, in cycles, on a net basis.
india-npci.access: TPAP, PSP bank, issuing bank, beneficiary bank and NPCI are distinct roles. App adoption is not direct central-bank account access.

lynx.title: Lynx
lynx.role: Payments Canada owns and operates Lynx. Direct participants must maintain eligible Bank of Canada settlement accounts.
lynx.method: RTGS-style high-value settlement in central-bank money
lynx.distinction: A high-value settlement system is not interchangeable with ACSS retail clearing.

acss.title: ACSS
acss.role: Payments Canada operates ACSS for retail payment items such as direct deposit, pre-authorized debits and cheque-related payments.
acss.method: Retail clearing with net settlement obligations at the Bank of Canada
acss.distinction: Batch retail processing should not be labelled a real-time gross settlement rail.

rtr.title: Real-Time Rail (RTR)
rtr.role: Payments Canada’s proposed national instant-payment infrastructure, separately governed from Interac e-Transfer.
rtr.method: Planned direct participation and settlement-access arrangements
rtr.distinction: As of October 30, 2026, the operator’s published launch target is not proof of live operation.

interac-e-transfer.title: Interac e-Transfer
interac-e-transfer.role: Interac operates e-Transfer; participating financial institutions provide the account relationships and customer balances.
interac-e-transfer.method: Distinct consumer service, connectivity arrangements and underlying clearing/settlement mechanisms
interac-e-transfer.distinction: Interac neither holds the transferred balance nor provides an independent central-bank settlement account to every app.

fedwire.title: Fedwire Funds Service
fedwire.role: Federal Reserve-operated high-value funds transfer system.
fedwire.method: Transfers settle via Federal Reserve account arrangements
fedwire.distinction: Fedwire is not the ACH network or the FedNow retail instant service.

fedach.title: FedACH
fedach.role: Federal Reserve Banks operate one of the two US ACH processing networks.
fedach.method: Batch ACH processing and interbank settlement as provided under ACH operator arrangements
fedach.distinction: Nacha is the ACH rules administrator, not the only system operator.

fednow.title: FedNow
fednow.role: Federal Reserve-developed infrastructure used by eligible participating financial institutions and technical providers.
fednow.method: Instant processing and settlement through appropriate Reserve Bank account arrangements
fednow.distinction: A software vendor certified for FedNow is not thereby a settlement account holder.

rtp.title: RTP network
rtp.role: Operated by The Clearing House, distinct from Federal Reserve’s FedNow.
rtp.method: Instant interbank clearing and settlement according to RTP arrangements
rtp.distinction: It is not interoperable with FedNow merely because both support instant payments.

chips.title: CHIPS
chips.role: The Clearing House operates CHIPS for high-value interbank USD payments.
chips.method: High-value interbank payment settlement under CHIPS rules
chips.distinction: CHIPS is not Fedwire, even though banks use both for high-value USD payments.

epn.title: Electronic Payments Network (EPN)
epn.role: The Clearing House operates EPN as the second national ACH operator alongside Federal Reserve Banks.
epn.method: Batch ACH processing under the shared ACH operating rules
epn.distinction: The operator is The Clearing House; Nacha is the rules administrator.

pix.title: Pix scheme
pix.role: BCB owns Pix, sets the rules and supervises scheme participation.
pix.method: Instant payment experience supported by SPI and DICT
pix.distinction: Pix the scheme is not the same object as SPI the settlement infrastructure.

spi.title: SPI settlement infrastructure
spi.role: BCB operates SPI to settle Pix between eligible direct participants.
spi.method: Real-time gross settlement in designated central-bank accounts
spi.distinction: A user-facing Pix institution may instead settle through a direct participant.

dict.title: DICT alias directory
dict.role: BCB operates the directory linking Pix keys to payment accounts.
dict.method: Address resolution rather than money movement or settlement
dict.distinction: A payment address directory does not hold balances.

faster-payments.title: Faster Payments
faster-payments.role: Pay.UK operates Faster Payments, while settlement occurs through the Bank of England’s RTGS.
faster-payments.method: Near-real-time customer payments; interbank net settlement in separate cycles
faster-payments.distinction: Customer funds being available immediately does not imply every transaction settled instantly at BoE.

bacs.title: Bacs
bacs.kind: Retail direct debit and credit clearing
bacs.role: Pay.UK operates the Bacs scheme for recurring credits and debits.
bacs.method: Multi-day retail processing with net settlement on Bank of England books
bacs.distinction: Do not confuse Bacs batch timing with Faster Payments availability.

chaps.title: CHAPS
chaps.role: The Bank of England operates CHAPS.
chaps.method: Real-time settlement in Bank of England RTGS
chaps.distinction: Not the same operator or model as Pay.UK’s Faster Payments.

boe-rtgs.title: Bank of England RTGS
boe-rtgs.role: Settlement accounts supporting CHAPS and net settlement for other sterling payment systems.
boe-rtgs.distinction: Not every company providing a customer-facing payment service holds its own BoE account.

upi.title: UPI
upi.role: NPCI owns and operates UPI; banks and third-party app providers perform different functions.
upi.method: Network-led interbank instructions and settlement arrangements via regulated institutions
upi.distinction: The app the customer uses, the bank account and the network operator should be separate nodes.
